sentences.text: This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award passed by the Senior Civil Judge & XIV Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Tiptur (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC.No.672/2011 dated 04.01.2014.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge & XIV Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Tiptur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy and meager compensation awarded by the tribunal.
2. Despite service of notice to respondents, they remained unrepresented.
Though this matter is listed for admission, it is taken-up for final disposal.
3. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

4. Brief facts of the case is as under:
On 09.01.2011 at about 1.00 a.m., the claimant was returning to Tiputur in a Bajaj motor bike bearing registration No.KA-02-K-5515 with his friend Anwar Pasha,
S/o.Ismail Sab after finishing the repair work of Maruthi van at Hindiskere gate,
Tiptur Taluk, on N.H.206, at that time, one TATA Sumo bearing registration No.KA-03-A-6563 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner with high speed coming from opposite side, dashed against the said Bajaj motor bike, in which claimant was a pillion rider, due to which, the claimant sustained injuries to all over the body.
Thereafter, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Tiptur, wherein he was inpatient for a period of 45 days.
During that period, he underwent operation on his left leg knee and steel rod was inserted to his left leg.
He has spent huge amount towards his treatment.

Due to the accident, he is unable to perform his duties as he was doing prior to the occurrence of accident, thereby he has incurred permanent physical disablement and has lost earning capacity, thereby creating dent in future Sri Fayaz Khan vs Sri Javid Pasha on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29066256/

sentences.text:
On service of notice, respondent No.1 appeared and did not file his statement of objections,
whereas, respondent No.2 remained absent.
6.
On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

7. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P8 whereas respondents neither examined the witnesses nor got marked any documents.
8. On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary, the tribunal awarded the compensation of `62,600/- and directed the respondents to pay the compensation.
Being aggrieved by the meager compensation amount awarded, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

9. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the amount awarded has been realised by filing an execution petition against the respondent-owner of the offending vehicle, in view of the admitted fact that there was no insurance for the said vehicle.
In the present case, admittedly, the occurrence of accident, involvement of vehicle, injuries sustained by the claimant are all proved by production of documents as per Exs.P1 to P8.
The charge sheet is laid against the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. TATA Sumo, which is not questioned and neither disputed.
There is no cross- appeal or cross-objection preferred by the owner of the offending vehicle.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellant- claimant, the points that would arise for consideration before this Court are:
i) Whether the claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?
ii) What order ?
11. Having perused the entire material evidence both oral and documentary and the impugned judgment and award, I am of the opinion that the tribunal has committed an error in awarding meager compensation thereby point Nos.1 and 2 are answered in the affirmative i.e. in favour of the claimant.
Therefore, the claimant would be entitled for marginal indulgence of enhancement of compensation for the reasons stated hereinbelow:
(a) It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 09.01.2011 at 1.00 a.m.
The involvement of the vehicle, occurrence of accident, injuries having been sustained by the claimant are all not disputed.
The question here is that what is the compensation of quantum that required to be awarded.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the claimant has sustained fracture of both bones of left leg.
It is also seen from the records that the claimant has not bothered to examine the Doctor and to produce the disability certificate.
Therefore, I deem it appropriate to enhance the same to Rs.50,000/-.
(c) The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.16,000/- under the head medical expenses, which is based on the actual bills produced by the claimant and the same is not interfered and is retained.

(d) The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,600/- and Rs.5,000/- under the heads attendant charges, extra nourishment, transportation and other incidental expenses respectively, which is on the lower side.

Therefore, I deem it appropriate to enhance the same to Rs.5,000/- and Rs.10,000/-
respectively.

(d) The tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/-, towards loss of income during laid up period,
which is on the lower side.
The accident having occurred in the year 2011, the notional income for the said period is prescribed as Rs.6,500/-.

Since the claimant has sustained fracture of two bones,
it would not be possible for him to get back to his work and three months would be required for recuperation and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore, `19,500/- (6,500x3) is awarded under this head.
(e) The tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head loss of amenities.
Therefore, I deem it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

(f) In view of the above discussions, the claimant is entitled to a total compensation of `1,29,500/-
as against `,62,600/- morefully mentioned in the table below:-
As awarded by this Head Court (`) Towards pain and suffering 50,000.00 Towards two simple injuries 4,000.00
Towards medical expenses 16,000.00 Towards attendant charges 5,000.00
Towards extra nourishment and transportation and other incidental 10,000.00 expenses
Towards loss of earning during 19,500.00 laid up period Towards loss of amenities 25,000.00
